verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's docs say feature flags can be enabled and disabled independently per environment (dev, staging, production), and that a toggle endpoint can switch flags in one or more environments. SDK Connections exist, giving read-only access to a subset of flag data, and a hands-on probe minted one; nothing states these keys are scoped to a single environment. Custom environments are listed only on a higher pricing tier. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that SDK keys/connections are scoped per environment, clarity on which environments are available on lower tiers, independent corroboration of environment isolation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage separate environments (dev/staging/prod) with independent flag states and scoped SDK keys

citations.quote: Use environments such as dev, staging, and production to enable or disable feature flags independently.
Feature flags can be enabled and disabled on a per-environment basis.
the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
The SDK Connection Endpoint provides readonly access to a subset of your feature flag data, just enough for the GrowthBook SDKs to assign values to users.
